Verdict written to `.devlooper/runs/2026-09-22T18-47-47-486Z/page/hero/iter-01/verdict.json`.

**Overall: 38/100** (desktop 45, tablet 38, mobile 38)

Two critical failures dominate:

1. **Hero imagery entirely absent at every breakpoint.** Figma's hero is a full-bleed image stage: a sky painting (`181:671`) behind a bottom-anchored vessel render (`247:655`). The build shows a flat grey gradient with nothing in it - roughly 600px of the frame below the lead is empty. Worth noting for the fixer: `asset-fetch-summary.json` records `hero-sky.png`, `hero-vessel.png` and `hero-vessel-front.png` as never downloaded (Figma MCP Starter-plan limit, then REST rate limit), so the assets themselves may have to be fetched manually before this can close.

2. **Wordmark collides with the headline on tablet and mobile.** The `-12px` optical tuck is a fixed px value tuned for the 108px desktop headline; at ~56px (tablet) and ~44px (mobile) it eats into the letterforms, so "clippership" is drawn through "AI compute at". Needs an em-based tuck or removal below 1024px.

What is right: fonts resolve correctly (Exposure 450 108px/108px, `-4.32px`; Matter Medium lead at 24px/28.32px; CTA label Matter SemiBold 14px), the NBSP line break survives, the split-opacity lead is present, and desktop vertical rhythm lands almost exactly on spec (title at 148px, lead top ~478px vs 476px derived, 383px measure closing on the 1344px content edge). Tablet and mobile have no Figma frame, so their adaptations were judged only for overflow, clipping and hierarchy - both are clean apart from the wordmark collision.
